decisions.note: Recent evolution-skill locator 47:110002211 is confirmed, but the exact JP title wording is not sufficiently exposed by the checked repository/public evidence; do not lock a poetic hot-spring title from the Chinese bridge alone.

Locator 47:200442 is verified as JP 隠れ蓑. The Japanese idiom refers to a concealing/invisibility cloak while also literally naming a straw raincoat; Vietnamese choices would preserve different parts of that image, so defer.
Locator 47:201232 is verified as JP 目くらまし. Plausible Vietnamese titles range from 'che mắt' to 'đánh lạc hướng'; defer until a system-consistent label for this visibility debuff is selected.
Locator 47:202672 is verified as JP 心弾んで. It describes an uplifted/buoyant feeling and admits several natural Vietnamese phrasings; do not freeze the Chinese one-word choice as canonical.
Locator 47:200432 is verified as the identical JP title 集中力. 'Tập trung' is concise, natural Vietnamese and unambiguous as the standard start-related skill name.
Locator 47:200233 is verified as JP 雨の日×. Preserve the game's weather-condition naming and the × grade marker directly.
Locator 47:200232 is verified as JP 雨の日○. 'Trời mưa○' is a direct stable system label and keeps the ○ marker unchanged.
Locator 47:200231 is verified as JP 雨の日◎. Use the same weather-term stem as the ○/× variants and preserve ◎.

Locator 47:102901211 is verified as JP 雪国仕込みの直滑降. The title combines a 'snow-country-trained' nuance with the established downhill-skill term 直滑降; defer until that skill-family terminology is reviewed consistently.
Locator 47:100291 is verified as JP ゆきあかり、おいかけて. This is a poetic unique-skill title ('chasing snow-light') whose rhythm and image have multiple natural Vietnamese treatments.
Locator 47:200242 is verified as JP 雪の日○. 'Trời tuyết○' mirrors the stable weather-condition naming used for the rain variants.
Locator 47:200241 is verified as JP 雪の日◎. Preserve the same stem as 雪の日○ and keep the ◎ grade marker.
Locator 47:107402211 is verified as JP 雪華の追い上げ. 雪華 is a literary snow-flower image and 追い上げ has race-specific comeback/closing nuance, leaving multiple defensible Vietnamese titles.

Locator 47:111801111 is verified as JP 雪魄氷姿, a classical four-character expression associated with pure, wintry elegance. A literal Hán-Việt reading would be opaque while freer Vietnamese loses the literary form, so defer.

Locator 47:105003111 is verified as JP ゼロレイテンシ (zero latency). 'Độ trễ bằng 0' is the standard Vietnamese technical meaning and fits the character's system-like naming without borrowing an English localization.

Locator 47:102101111 is verified as JP 雷騰雲奔. The compact literary compound evokes thunder and rushing clouds; both Sino-Vietnamese and image-based translations are possible, so defer rather than lock an opaque calque.

Locator 47:106101111 is verified as JP 電撃の撫で切り, whose meaning is closer to an electric sweeping cut than the Chinese wording suggests. Because the bridge substantially rephrases the image, defer and translate from JP only after style review.
Locator 47:204101 is verified as the identical JP four-character title 震天動地. 'Chấn thiên động địa' is the established Vietnamese Hán-Việt idiom and preserves the compact literary form.

decisions.target_vi: Phi nước đại rung chuyển mặt đất
decisions.note: Locator 47:411041 is verified as JP 大地を揺るがす疾走. The Vietnamese title keeps the concrete image of a furious run shaking the ground and avoids relying on the Chinese phrasing.

Locator 47:102303211 is verified as JP ネオンの尾を引いて. The title describes leaving a neon trail/tail behind; several concise Vietnamese renderings fit, so defer until the visual-tech naming style is reviewed consistently.
